note: Client risk-assessment settings. No money questions: every item is an everyday-life read on how much risk the person takes, on a 1-5 scale (1 very cautious, 3 no strong preference, 5 very bold). Questions are re-rolled in a fresh order every visit; the 5 answer options are always shown in the same fixed order (Strongly disagree first, Strongly agree last) so the scale reads like a normal rating. 'type r' items are reversed (agreeing is cautious, so they score LOW when you agree) — they are what stop an always-agree clicker from looking bold. Distractors ('type d') carry weight 0. Bands are a team-parked starting table, not yet reviewed.
_record_endpoint_note: Paste your Google Apps Script web-app URL here to auto-log results to the team sheet. Leave empty for manual-code-only mode. Setup: team/SETUP.md

questions.text: I usually try a new thing before others do.
I make big decisions even when I'm missing some information.
I enjoy a bet when I think I have an edge.
If something doesn't work out, I try it again right away.
I start new projects even when the result is uncertain.
I'm the first to try an unfamiliar restaurant or product.
I buy new products the day they launch.
I take up new skills or hobbies on my own initiative.
A small chance at a big reward is worth taking.
I'd rather a riskier result with more upside than a safer smaller one.
When I'm unsure, I trust my own judgment over others' advice.
I act on a good idea before others think it is certain.
I carry an umbrella on a sunny day, in case it rains.
When I'm unsure, I choose the safer option.
I keep more of a thing than I need, so I never run out.
I would rather be certain of a smaller result than risk a bigger one.
I plan my week the night before.
I check the time a few times a day.
I have at least two cups of tea or coffee a day.
In my free time I read more than I watch.

_formula_note: Ranking weights are NOT a hand-picked table anymore: every parameter is a straight line weight = base + slope x G, where G = risk score / 100 (0 very cautious, 1 very growth-oriented). Calmness falls exactly as growth rises; the lines are normalized to sum to 100, rounded to 5s. Bands below only provide the client-facing label + style line.

weight_formula._shape: base = the weight for a fully-cautious client (score 0), slope = how it moves by score 100. Calm/safe params (vol, sharpe, beta, tracking) start high and fall; growth/skill params (CAGR, info ratio, selectivity) start near zero and rise. Picked so both ends sum to 100. Cost was replaced by beta (market sensitivity): expense-ratio data is unavailable (n/a for all funds), but beta is computed for every fund — a cautious client's list favours funds that fall less than the market.

bands.name: Conservative
bands.client_style: Your answers say you would rather see your money grow slowly but surely, than watch it bounce around. So we picked funds that stay calm even when the market is wild.

bands.name: Moderately Conservative
bands.client_style: You're okay with your money going up and down a little, but not a lot. We picked funds that grow a bit more than calm ones, while still not swinging too hard.

bands.name: Balanced
bands.client_style: You don't get nervous when markets wobble, and you're happy to wait out a bad year for a good result. We picked funds that mix steady parts with growth parts.

bands.name: Moderately Growth-Oriented
bands.client_style: You want real growth, and you're fine with the money dipping now and then to get it. We picked funds that aim higher and are built to take the bumps.

bands.name: Growth-Oriented
bands.client_style: You're after the biggest growth you can get, and small dips don't shake you. We picked funds that run at full speed — the biggest movers, held through the rough parts too.
